Hello,

I'm launching The Collatz Conjecture Challenge (ccchallenge.org), whose goal is to collaboratively formalise papers on the Collatz conjecture.

The governance model is hopefully simple (ccchallenge.org/method):

  • Anyone can add a paper to the formalisation goal
  • Anyone can add a formalisation to a paper (proof assistant agnostic)
  • Anyone can write an audit report on a formalisation (assessing if it's faithful to the paper)

AI can be used but needs to be disclosed, and, for audit reports, we require that the human authors of the report are fully accountable for its conclusions.

See:

  • https://ccchallenge.org/story
  • https://ccchallenge.org/method
  • https://ccchallenge.org/contribute

Feedback and contributions welcome :))!

Hello, thank you for your interest! The way we currently operate is to audit formalisations attached to a write up of some form (e.g. arxiv paper). If you have one, don't hesitate to add it to the list of papers on ccchallenge.org and link your formalisation to it :)

Hi Tristan,

I may be interested in this. I am worried I will be stuck at the arxiv part; I am an unpublished nanophysicist so I do not have publishing allowance in mathematics at arxiv, and the Collatz is notoriously difficult to broach as a subject to professional mathematicians, who generally will immediately assume one is a crackpot. Is anyone in your group able to give endorsements? I should have a new paper written before too long describing my lean4 project, my code is approaching completion.
I would look at the paper (maybe even contribute to formalization) but my last math.NT/CO preprints are too long ago for endorsement priviledges.
I'm probably gonna go for discrete systems rather than NT, its a better fit to be honest. But thanks Ralf, I will keep you in mind.
